summary: Girdon's wardens on the Grey Ford: truce or feud, the river's wealth, three friends, the host and the sea question.

long_feuds_toll.name: The Long Feud's Toll
long_feuds_toll.desc: Half a century of war with Gunwaith left a grave in every village by the river. The wardens are tired of it and ready for it, and both feelings run in the same men.

wardens_of_the_river.name: Wardens of the River
wardens_of_the_river.desc: The assembly speaks with one voice, and the wardens obey it. Each ford has its captain, each captain has his orders, and nobody has to ask twice.

ford_defenders.name: Defenders of the Ford
ford_defenders.desc: When the truce broke, the wardens were at the water before the first banner crossed. They know every stone of the ford and every hollow of the bank.

parims_coin.name: Parim's Coin
parims_coin.desc: Aenoran gold arrives at Girdon in small, regular purses. It pays for useful things, and everyone in the river towns knows what it buys.

kings_guarantee.name: The King's Guarantee
kings_guarantee.desc: A letter under the royal seal declares that Girdon's borders will be defended by the crown in Parim. The wardens are not sure they want defending, but the letter sits on the council table.

council_league.name: A League of Councils
council_league.desc: Girdon and Corogon have pledged to stand together, one at the fords and one at the quays. Their envoys travel freely in each other's land.

river_will_not_bend.name: The River Will Not Bend
river_will_not_bend.desc: The river has run in one bed since before the first town was built, and Girdon means to stand on its bank as long. Every ford is mined with stakes, and every bridge is ready to fall.

warden_drill.name: Wardens' Drill
warden_drill.desc: Aldo Ferrin has taught the wardens to hold a shield-wall in a river's current. They stand, they shove and they do not break.

commission_proposal.title: Girdon Proposes a Commission
commission_proposal.desc: Riders from Girdon have come to the court with a proposal: a Ford Commission, of three wardens and three thanes, to walk the river each spring and settle every dispute before it becomes a raid. They say the truce will not hold without one.

brotherhood_offer.title: Brothers Across the Ford?
brotherhood_offer.desc: A warden of Girdon stands at our end of the Grey Ford with his hands empty. His lady proposes that the two realms swear brotherhood, and that the river become a border for trade and not for war. Many of our thanes have buried kinsmen on the far bank.

options.name: Not while the dead of the ford lie unburied

parims_friendship.title: The River Wardens Seek Parim's Friendship
parims_friendship.desc: A deputation from Girdon has arrived in Parim, humbly dressed and carrying a letter from the Warden-Speaker. She asks for the crown's protection against the long quarrel with Gunwaith, and for the favour of a king who has the gold to be generous.

council_pact.title: A Pact of Councils
council_pact.desc: Girdon's wardens write that the two council realms have much in common: harbours and fords, merchants and wardens, a dislike of kings and a long list of quarrels with Aenor. They propose a pact, each to guarantee the other.

focuses.name: The Wardens' Assembly
focuses.desc: Girdon is governed by an assembly of river-wardens who elect a Warden-Speaker. Pernia Lothor signed the Truce of the Grey Ford, and the assembly has stood behind her ever since.

focuses.name: The Truce Party
focuses.desc: A wing of the assembly believes the truce is the best thing that has happened to Girdon in fifty years, and wishes to protect it. Their speakers are heard, and their bread is baked.

focuses.name: The Old Feud Party
focuses.desc: Another wing remembers the dead, and wishes to keep their grievances sharp. Its speakers are loud, and the river towns listen to them with half an ear.

focuses.name: Pernia's Seal
focuses.desc: Pernia Lothor presses her seal on a charter that gives the assembly one voice in the face of the other. It is not a perfect peace, but it is a working one.

focuses.name: The Assembly United
focuses.desc: The assembly votes as one, on the ford and on everything else. The old quarrel between the two parties is shelved, and the wardens find that they can govern after all.

focuses.name: The Ford Wardens
focuses.desc: The Grey Ford is the one place where the river can be crossed on foot, and wardens have held it since the truce. They are brave, patient and very bored.

focuses.name: Propose a Commission
focuses.desc: The assembly sends a proposal to Gunwaith: let three wardens and three thanes walk the river each spring. Perhaps it can keep the peace better than the truce can.

focuses.name: Walls at the Ford
focuses.desc: A stone wall rises on the near bank, with a gate that can be shut in a quarter of an hour. Nobody in Girdon calls it an act of war, though nobody on the other bank believes them.

focuses.name: The Blood-Price
focuses.desc: Girdon offers a blood-price for each of the dead whose killers are known. It is an old custom, and it costs a great deal, and families on both banks come to the gate to collect.

focuses.name: Defend the Ford
focuses.desc: The truce is broken and Gunwaith's war-thanes are across the water. The wardens go to the ford with spears and shields, because that is what the ford is for.

focuses.name: A Lasting Peace
focuses.desc: The commission walks the river, hears the claims and records the settlements. For a season, the ford is quiet, and nobody can say the peace is only a pause.

focuses.name: The Winter Ford Remembered
focuses.desc: In the dead of winter a stranger stood at the ford and held the crossing for the refugees. The wardens tell the story to children, and carve the date on a stone.

focuses.name: Peace on the River
focuses.desc: The feud is over, and the river runs peacefully between its banks. Girdon has been through the worst of it, and means to build something better.

focuses.name: River Barges
focuses.desc: Long flat barges ply the river from the hills to the sea. The wardens dredge the shallows and mend the locks, and the barge-masters pay a toll.

focuses.name: The Mills of Girdon
focuses.desc: Water-wheels line the river like a necklace. They grind grain, saw timber and drive hammers, and Corla Wend counts every turn of them in her ledgers.

focuses.name: River Tolls
focuses.desc: Every barge that passes a lock pays a copper. The wardens collect it at the gate, and the assembly spends it on the fords.

focuses.name: The River-Mouth Yards
focuses.desc: Where the river meets the sea, shipwrights set up slips for sea-going hulls. Girdon has never built ships before, and builds them well.

focuses.name: The Wardens' Arsenal
focuses.desc: A great forge-hall is raised behind the river wall, where smiths make spear-heads, shield-bosses and mail. The wardens carry what they have forged.

focuses.name: Girdon's Friends
focuses.desc: Girdon cannot stand alone for ever, and the wardens know it. The assembly sends envoys to every court that might offer a hand.

focuses.name: Brothers Across the Ford
focuses.desc: The Warden-Speaker proposes a brotherhood with Gunwaith, which was her enemy and may be her neighbour in peace. It is a hard thing to ask of those with a grave in every village.

focuses.name: Parim's Old Friend
focuses.desc: The crown in Parim has deep pockets and long memories. Girdon sends a deputation to ask for its old friendship, and the king is said to be pleased.

focuses.name: The Southern Councils
focuses.desc: Corogon is also a council realm, with harbours where Girdon has fords. The two assemblies exchange letters, and each finds the other's complaints familiar.

focuses.name: The River League Answered
focuses.desc: Gunwaith has clasped hands, and a league of the two river-realms takes shape. Wardens and thanes share a table, and the old quarrel is spoken of in the past tense.

focuses.name: The King's Guarantee
focuses.desc: A guarantee under the royal seal arrives at Girdon in a leather case. It says that the crown will answer any attack on the river, and the wardens read it more than once.

focuses.name: A League of Councils
focuses.desc: Delegates from Girdon and Corogon sit side by side at a long table. The rivermen and the seamen drink each other's health.

focuses.name: The River Will Not Bend
focuses.desc: Whatever friends Girdon has made, the river is Girdon's own, and its wardens will defend it. The stakes go in, the walls go up and the assembly votes again to hold.

focuses.name: Warden Companies
focuses.desc: Each river town raises a company of wardens, with its own banner and its own captain. They drill on the green and march to the ford at the drum.

focuses.name: River Bows
focuses.desc: Wardens learn to shoot from the bank at a boat in the current. The best archers are given a banner and a feast day.

focuses.name: Pike and Shield
focuses.desc: The wardens carry a long pike for the front rank and a round shield for the rear. They are hard to break, and harder to outflank.

focuses.name: Aldo's Wardens
focuses.desc: Warden-Captain Aldo Ferrin learned the shield-wall from the old river-masters and now drills their sons. He puts the companies in a line along the river and tells them where to stand.

focuses.name: The River Levy
focuses.desc: Every household within a day's march of the river is called on for a man. The levy is a hard thing, and it has never been a long one.

focuses.name: A Delegate to the Ford Council
focuses.desc: Girdon sends a warden to sit at the Ford Council. She is to listen, to speak when the river is mentioned, and to count how many seats are on each side.

focuses.name: The Wardens Cross
focuses.desc: The council has chosen, and the wardens are called. They take ship at the river-mouth yards, with bows strung and shields on their backs.

focuses.name: Girdon Sends Ships
focuses.desc: The yards at the river mouth send their first hulls to the fleet. They are small, and they are green, and they are Girdon's own.

focuses.name: Wardens Beyond the Sea
focuses.desc: Some wardens did not come home. Their captains hold a ruined town beyond the sea, and now they have a banner to rally to.

focuses.name: Wardens for the Relief
focuses.desc: The west sails to relieve the Middle Lands, and Girdon sends its wardens to stand beside the Aenoran levy. They do not love the crown, but they love the dead less.

focuses.name: Home from the Sea
focuses.desc: The ships come home, or they do not, and the wardens count who is missing. In this telling the river is quiet, and the ford has been mended.
